text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions, so variables and functions have meaningful names that explain their purpose. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to follow and easier to test. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because when problems appear, developers can find and fix them quickly. In short, writing clean code saves time and helps teams work together more effectively.
